video_title: The LaMelo Ball Trade! | The Jon Krawczynski Show

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Wolves' interest in acquiring LaMelo Ball from the Hornets
quotes.excerpt: It's LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves, Naz Reid and draft pick compensation is going out the door.

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: It started to percolate that maybe the Wolves have a little bit of interest in LaMelo Ball and I asked you to come on and I figured, we will just talk a little bit through some of the possibilities and lo and behold, we both wake up this morning and the deal is done. It's LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves, Naz Reid and draft pick compensation is going out the door.

text_blocks.speaker: Dane Moore
text_blocks.text: The first time I knew it was a possibility was when you said, hey Dane, you want to come on my podcast tomorrow morning? And I said, what are we going to talk about? You said LaMelo and I was like, oh, okay, so this is happening.

quotes.speaker: Dane Moore
quotes.summary_phrase: Impact of trading Naz Reid for LaMelo Ball
quotes.excerpt: I didn't expect the Naz Reid part of it. It looked like that opportunity was going to be there.
quotes.quote: I didn't expect the Naz Reid part of it. I think from a Timberwolves perspective, he is the longest-tenured Timberwolf. You and I have known him for a very long time. Awesome guy, somebody that I wanted to see come into full flower and it looked like that opportunity was going to be there without Julius Randle. So that was the first thing when I saw the Shams tweet when I was like, oh, Naz, it's Naz, it's not Rudy, which was kind of the framework I thought it was going to end up being.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves' long-term interest in pairing LaMelo Ball with Anthony Edwards
quotes.excerpt: Tim Connelly and Chris Finch have long believed that LaMelo Ball is a perfect fit for Anthony Edwards.
quotes.quote: I think Tim Connelly and Chris Finch have long believed that LaMelo Ball is a perfect fit for Anthony Edwards in that backcourt. And I know that over the last several years, they have checked in on LaMelo and Charlotte a couple of times. Hey, would you do this? Would you do that for LaMelo? Each time they were turned away. And so something has happened in the last couple of days, weeks to get the Charlotte Hornets to a point where they were comfortable parting with LaMelo Ball.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Risks associated with the LaMelo Ball acquisition
quotes.excerpt: There is a little bit of an element of risk involved from the Wolves' perspective.
quotes.quote: There is a little bit of an element of risk involved from the Wolves' perspective because he hasn't stayed healthy except for last year. And then he also has not played in the playoffs yet and has I think some questions about his maturity. But when you look at where his game is at right now, man, it just seems like a really good timing for him on that front.

quotes.speaker: Dane Moore
quotes.summary_phrase: Understanding the inherent risk in acquiring star players
quotes.excerpt: The Wolves, given how few draft assets that they have, they weren't able to go get a player.
quotes.quote: We knew that risk was going to happen in any of these moves. The Wolves, given how few draft assets that they have, they weren't able to go get a player who doesn't come with risk. And that's why we spent so much time over the past month or so talking about players who have varying levels of risk like Kyrie Irving. We spent a lot of time on there was going to be risk associated with that. Obviously Ja Morant and LaMelo, there is that as well.

quotes.speaker: Dane Moore
quotes.summary_phrase: The Timberwolves' shift toward a younger roster
quotes.excerpt: It's a really, really young team. There's only two guys on the team that are in their thirties.
quotes.quote: It's a really, really young team. I think there's only two guys on the team that are in their thirties, right? Rudy and Dante DiVincenzo who is not going to play. Also, LaMelo, three years left on his contract. Anthony Edwards, three years left on his contract. Jaden McDaniels, three years left on his contract. Jovan Barron, three years left on his contract. We always talked about the second window, the second window of the Anthony Edwards era, like this is it. This is this three years with those four guys.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: LaMelo Ball's status as the best player among the core
quotes.excerpt: If you want to put LaMelo Ball, Kyrie Irving coming off of an injury, and Ja Morant in a bucket.
quotes.quote: If you want to put LaMelo Ball, Kyrie Irving coming off of an injury, and Ja Morant in a bucket, LaMelo Ball is the best player of the three of them right now, I think. Maybe Kyrie, you could say, but with his age and his injury, we don't know how he's coming off of that. I think LaMelo Ball is better than Ja Morant. Yeah, there are going to be times where we're watching next season and he pulls one from eight with 18 seconds on the shot clock from 40 feet and you're going to be like, what is he doing?

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: LaMelo Ball's positive impact on offensive efficiency
quotes.excerpt: They were plus 11.1 on offensive efficiency with him on the floor plus 9.9 overall.
quotes.quote: Looking at cleaning the glass, they were plus 11.1 on offensive efficiency with him on the floor plus 9.9 overall. Those are like enormous numbers. And I do think it is something that as someone who hasn't watched LaMelo every day, I looked at it like, man, is this guy a winning player? Does he do the right things? But a lot of last season, he did a lot of those things.

quotes.speaker: Dane Moore
quotes.summary_phrase: Significance of the 2033 unprotected first-round pick in the trade
quotes.excerpt: The big, the big pick is the 2033 unprotected first-round pick.
quotes.quote: The big, the big pick is the 2033 unprotected first-round pick. And in 2033 is certainly a long ways, longer than the three years that they have all these guys under contract. Like if I'm Charlotte, I'm looking at that like that's a nice pick. That will be a nice pick. But it's seven years down the line. I do think from an opportunity cost standpoint, like you could have maybe traded that pick so distant into the future for, you know, maybe two first-round picks more closely and then you don't necessarily need to go all in.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: The Timberwolves' aggressive pursuit of star players
quotes.excerpt: It's Kevin Durant, it's Giannis Antetokounmpo, it's Kyrie Irving, it's all of these guys.
quotes.quote: It's Kevin Durant, it's Giannis Antetokounmpo, it's Kyrie Irving, it's all of these guys. And I can tell you, just in talking to people, they were in on Jaylen Brown as well. Jaylen Brown was, it was made clear by the Celtics that he was going to be available and the Wolves were trying to have conversations about what it would take to get Jaylen Brown. I think that they looked at those two, Jaylen Brown and LaMelo Ball, and Brown just because he's won a championship, he's a little older, he, you know, was top six MVP this year, I think that the Celtics were asking more for Brown than what the Hornets wanted for Ball.

quotes.speaker: Dane Moore
quotes.summary_phrase: Salary cap implications of the LaMelo Ball trade
quotes.excerpt: In this trade, the Wolves are taking on LaMelo Ball and Josh Green.
quotes.quote: In this trade, the Wolves are taking on LaMelo Ball and Josh Green and that's like $56 million of salary. That's what Jaylen Brown makes, right? He makes $57 million. So they could have done the same sort of out salary match mechanics in that way. But I will note that Jaylen Brown is under contract for three years $183 million and LaMelo Ball is under contract for three years $130 million. We're talking about Jaylen Brown is on the supermax 35% of the cap. LaMelo Ball is making 25% of the cap.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Projecting the Timberwolves' starting lineup
quotes.excerpt: Are we assuming like the starting lineup on opening night as of right now is Rudy at the 5.
quotes.quote: Are we assuming like the starting lineup on opening night as of right now is Rudy at the 5, Jaden at the 4, Jovan at the 3, Ant at the 2, LaMelo at the 1, is that what you're thinking?

quotes.speaker: Dane Moore
quotes.summary_phrase: The necessity of trading for a power forward
quotes.excerpt: All of this mechanics could have worked for Jaylen Brown and gotten that deal in.
quotes.quote: All of this mechanics could have worked for Jaylen Brown and gotten that deal in. But Boston was not going to take just Naz Reid and picks for Jaylen Brown. And so I think, I'm just guessing at this, but my speculation is that it would have required Rudy, Naz, and maybe even like Shannon or someone else and picks for Jaylen Brown and that just was not going to be a realistic thing.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: The Timberwolves' roster composition and future moves
quotes.excerpt: You part with Naz, beloved and a valuable part, but you still have Rudy.
quotes.quote: You part with Naz, beloved and a valuable part, but you still have Rudy who I think is going to be critical for him defensively to help LaMelo Ball out. And you also have Terrence Shannon Jr., you have Jovan, you have a lot of your young players still in in the fold here. But to your point on the larger issue, yeah, I do think that they still they need a power forward right now, today, you would say, it is. It's LaMelo, Ant, and it's then Jaden at the 4 and Rudy at the 5.

quotes.speaker: Dane Moore
quotes.summary_phrase: Potential power forward targets for the Timberwolves
quotes.excerpt: I've heard Sandro Mamukelashvili from Toronto as as potentially an option there.
quotes.quote: I've heard Sandro Mamukelashvili from Toronto as as potentially an option there. Now, I think that's going to depend on what his free agent market place ends up being and I'm not sure if the Wolves like will be able to compete from an offer standpoint of what that is. But, you know, that would be a way to kind of repurpose a little bit of the, you know, he has some of the floor spacing element that Naz had and he can play off the second side to attack a closeout, those sort of things.

quotes.speaker: Dane Moore
quotes.summary_phrase: The Timberwolves' need for a backup big man
quotes.excerpt: They need to make an additional move like this roster.
quotes.quote: They need to make an additional move like this roster is also a little bit incomplete and maybe we should talk about that a little bit. You had too many power forwards, you know, 72 hours ago on this team and now you have none. And and that's the the kind of the curiosity when I try to picture this. I know we we could talk about LaMelo a little bit more, but I do think we should talk about, you know, who's the starting power forward?

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of LaMelo Ball's availability on the Timberwolves' financial strategy
quotes.excerpt: I do believe that LaMelo Ball's availability changed the course of where the Wolves were going to go.
quotes.quote: I do believe that LaMelo Ball's availability changed the course of where the Wolves were going to go from a financial aspect. Now, when they made the trade and and salary dump Julius Randle, they were under the tax entirely and out of the tax. And I do think that there were avenues that they were exploring to stay out of the tax. You know, you could have even made a Jaylen Brown deal and stayed out of the tax if it but if you were willing to part with Rudy and Naz and and a bunch of other things. But, from what I'm told, from high-level sources within the Wolves, it's that when LaMelo Ball became available, Mark Lore, Alex Rodriguez got fully behind this and said, that's fine. Yep, let's pay it. Let's go into the tax again.

quotes.speaker: Dane Moore
quotes.summary_phrase: The competitive advantage of paying the luxury tax
quotes.excerpt: Paying the teams, if you're competitive, you should pay the luxury tax.
quotes.quote: Paying the teams, if you're competitive, you should pay the luxury tax. Where it starts getting gray is when you've been in the luxury tax for multiple seasons in a row as the Timberwolves have. They've I think there's paid like $110 million in luxury tax right over the last two seasons. And now, like, I mean, it kind of depends where the the final spending ends up being, but I think you're talking about another sizable luxury tax bill that they'll that they'll be taking on here.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves' search for shooting and power forward depth
quotes.excerpt: I think they're going to look at two things. You will look at power forward.
quotes.quote: I think they're going to look at two things. You will look at power forward. I also do think they're going to look to add more shooting. You know, they got Isaiah Evans in the draft, but, you know, Dante DiVincenzo is going to be out for much of next season. I will say too, another little point, I was told that they do not want to trade Dante DiVincenzo still. So that the plan is to keep him, rehab him, and get him back on the floor sometime this season. Plans can change, but as of right now, they do not envision trading Dante DiVincenzo.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Reflecting on Naz Reid's development and legacy with the Timberwolves
quotes.excerpt: There has never been a better development story in in this team's history, I don't think.
quotes.quote: There has never been a better development story in in this team's history, I don't think. I mean, he comes in as this pudgy, kind of injured guy from LSU that's undrafted. You don't know is he a 5, is he a 4, what can he do? And man, this guy just constantly every single year changed his body, changed, you know, added to his game, was completely selfless in being a sixth man behind Karl-Anthony Towns, behind Julius Randle, and over and over and again delivered for these guys. And I there's few players who I have more affection for over these 22 years than Naz. I will be very sorry to see him go.
